records.name: Jovars
records.facts_used: Jovars: The agency documents Lithuanian Jovaras rendered as Latvian Jovars. The Lithuanian name is based on the tree word jovaras. That word is applied to several tree species, so poplar alone would be too narrow a translation; the tree-name link is firmer than selecting a single species. The Latvian Language Agency gives the exact rendering Jovaras → Jovars, citing page 47 of a 1961 manual. This dated record illustrates transmission between languages; it is not a first birth registration or proof of one borrowing route in every family.
records.reason: Exact-form or explicitly scoped family evidence supports two paragraphs in five languages.
records.uncertainties: Exact rendering establishes one documented route, not every bearer’s borrowing path. Tree-word polysemy preserved; catalogue contradictory unambiguous-species sentence rejected. Exact agency HTML record https://www.personvarduatveide.lv/words/19282?locale=lv was opened; the cited printed manual page was not independently reopened unless separately noted. Opened LKŽ mirror entry confirms several tree-species senses, not one unambiguous species.

records.name: Ksaveras
records.facts_used: Ksaveras: Lithuanian Ksaveras belongs to the Xavier family. Its base is the Basque place name Etxaberri, from etxe, house, and berri, new. The personal name’s history involves a transferred place name rather than translation from a similar-sounding Lithuanian word. The 1964 calendar reprinted in Salys’s 1983 volume gives Pranciškus Ksaveras (Pranas, Pranys) on 3 December. This is a concrete printed example of the form’s use. Its position in the historical calendar need not match every modern calendar and is not the name’s invention date.
